clue.text: Damage resulting from small change in the earth

indicators.note: the coin is set inside the ground, so one piece sits in the other

parts.note: the earth means soil, the ground
P is a penny, the smallest coin

explanation.surface: Damage done to the ground by some slight alteration in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small change' looks like a minor alteration; it is a penny, P, placed in SOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin or mar something is a synonym for damaging it.

clue.text: Wrapping up well, .put on pounds — move around!

indicators.note: around has the movement word surrounding the added weight

parts.note: to swing is to move to and fro
to put on is to add
L is the abbreviation for pounds (libra)

explanation.surface: Bundled up, you put on weight, so get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on pounds' reads as weight gain; it is ADD plus L, set inside SWING.
explanation.definitionFit: Binding a baby tightly in cloths is a way of wrapping it snugly.

clue.text: To put up with the woman is the only alternative

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the short word is written upwards

parts.note: the word written as it stands
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Tolerating the woman is the only option left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To put up with' reads as 'tolerate'; 'put up' turns TO into OT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A different, remaining choice is the alternative one.

clue.text: Giving a winger encouragement is a bloomer

parts.note: a lark is a bird, something with wings
a spur is an incentive or encouragement

explanation.surface: Cheering on a wing player is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, and 'winger' a footballer; here they are a flower and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This delphinium is a flowering plant, something that blooms.

clue.text: In a deadlock few will be calm

indicators.note: In tells us the small number goes inside the stalemate word

parts.note: an impasse is a deadlock, a situation with no way forward
IV is four in Roman numerals, a few

explanation.surface: Staying composed when negotiations reach stalemate.
explanation.walkthrough: IV goes into IMPASSE after IMPASS, with the E at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no emotion means being unruffled and composed.

clue.text: Hostelries in the capitals of Norway and Sweden

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: capitals here means the initial letters of the two country names, not their cities

explanation.surface: Hotels in Oslo and Stockholm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' wants Oslo and Stockholm; it means initial letters N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Places offering lodging and drink to travellers.

clue.text: The head taking in a fool — one over enthusiastic

indicators.note: taking in means the head word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
an ass is a fool
I is the Roman numeral one
on can mean over, as in a lid on a box

explanation.surface: A headmaster takes on a fool, someone over-keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head' suggests a headteacher; it is PATE, holding ASS, I and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent and fervent, full of strong feeling.

clue.text: Trim a tree for Christmas?

definitions.meaning: a conifer commonly used as a Christmas tree

explanation.definitionFit: Neat and smart is one sense; the Norway conifer used at Christmas is the other.

clue.text: Eating in, so get the ingredients

annotationWithheld.why: Eating in, so get the ingredients (9): an anagram of 'in, so get' gives only seven letters; INGESTION needs IN as well, so 'in' would do two jobs or the clue is short
annotationWithheld.clue: Eating in, so get the ingredients

clue.text: A girl in excellent health

indicators.note: in signals the name is concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: A young woman in fine fettle.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Supporters rent a shed perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of these words could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Backers of a cause hire a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of a party or cause are its backers.

clue.text: Referring to a young woman as a queen

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in a business letter
a gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Calling a young lady a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal in manner, befitting a monarch.

clue.text: Coercion is socially acceptable in the outfit

indicators.note: in places the letter for acceptability inside the clothing word

parts.note: a dress is an outfit of clothing
U means upper-class, socially acceptable, in British usage

explanation.surface: Forcing people into dressing the right way.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'upper class, acceptable' is a British convention from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure by threat or force is compulsion.

clue.text: Passes on article about a man of authority, a bishop

indicators.note: about means the dying word wraps around the officer

parts.note: to pass on is to die, so dies
OC is Officer Commanding, a man in authority
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone dies, and a newspaper article about a powerful man follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes on' looks like handing over; it is death, DIES, round OC, then AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocesan is the bishop in charge of a diocese.

clue.text: Like the vicar of Bray he is a prisoner

definitions.meaning: the vicar of Bray, in an English folk song, switched beliefs with each monarch to keep his living: an opportunist
a convict is one serving a sentence

explanation.definitionFit: An opportunist who bends with prevailing views is one sense; one serving a jail sentence is the other.

clue.text: A count is in error, but not at all concerned

indicators.note: in error says the letters of these words are wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: Someone miscounts but doesn't care a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges A COUNT IS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree and nonchalant, showing no worry.

clue.text: Yellow invertebrate

explanation.definitionFit: Cowardly, lacking courage, is one sense; literally lacking a backbone is the other.

clue.text: Long to make deal

definitions.meaning: to long is to yearn for something
deal is softwood timber such as fir or similar conifer wood

explanation.definitionFit: Yearn is one sense; the conifer timber called deal is the other.

clue.text: Source of income for working men (not wed)

indicators.note: working means these letters are being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Single men who work earn their living.
explanation.definitionFit: A fund or bequest that provides a regular revenue.

clue.text: A warring opponent

parts.note: read 'a-warring' as 'war-ing': someone opposed to war rather than an enemy in battle

explanation.definitionFit: One who rejects war and violence is an objector to fighting.

clue.text: Fortitude is called for on icy roads

definitions.meaning: fine gravel spread on frozen roads for traction

explanation.definitionFit: Courage is one sense; the sandy gravel spread on winter roads is the other.

clue.text: About a quarter took another course — so prudent

indicators.note: About means the retraining word surrounds the compass point

parts.note: retrained means went through another training course
S, south, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone retrained after a quarter, which was sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'approximately'; it wraps RETRAINED round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing self-control and moderation, holding back.

clue.text: The little swine loudly quarrel

parts.note: F is forte, loudly in music
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: Piglets squabble noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' looks like a row; it is a crossbow bolt, ARROW, after F.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter of piglets, a sow's young.

clue.text: Received rise and cheered

definitions.meaning: given a promotion or raised up

explanation.definitionFit: Raised in rank is one sense; elated or exhilarated is the other.

clue.text: Provide the points to be settled

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
due means owing, to be paid

explanation.surface: Supply the issues that need resolving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points to be settled' reads as issues; it is E and N then DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish or bestow a quality on someone.

clue.text: "As true a lover as ever sigh'd upon a midnight ---" (A.Y.L..1.)

definitions.text: "As true a lover as ever sigh'd upon a midnight ---" (A.Y.L..1.)

parts.words: "As true a lover as ever sigh'd upon a midnight ---" (A.Y.L..1.)
parts.note: a quotation from Shakespeare's As You Like It with its last word missing: what a lovesick man sighs on at night

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's comedy with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: A.Y.L.I. is As You Like It; Silvius speaks of a lover sighing on his bedding at midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the cushion a sleepless lover sighs upon at night.

clue.text: Take instruction and get list about right

indicators.note: about means the leaning word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: to list is to lean, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Study and get a list of facts right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' looks like a roll of items; it is a ship's tilt, LEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To study and acquire knowledge is to be taught.

clue.text: Load nothing before sun-rise

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the star word is written upwards

parts.note: the word written as it stands

explanation.surface: Carry nothing before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sun-rise' looks like dawn; 'rise' reverses SUN to NUS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or responsibility is a load to bear.

clue.text: Having a large number to bring up can be dispiriting

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
to rear is to bring up a child

explanation.surface: Raising a big family can be depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal and gloomy, sapping one's spirits.

clue.text: Against show, that's clear

parts.note: V is versus, against
to indicate is to show

explanation.surface: Opposing a display makes things plain.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to clear them of blame.

clue.text: Edward's replacing dunderhead with a good man as per direction

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter of the name is swapped for something new

parts.note: the name written as it stands
dunderhead is the head, the first letter, of dunder
taken as written
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A fool's name is swapped for that of a saintly man, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' is not an idiot but the first letter of dunder, D, which A and ST replace in EDWARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Going in the direction of the sunrise is a compass heading.

clue.text: Doctrine that might well be retrogressive

indicators.note: a word read backwards that comes out unchanged, so going back makes no difference

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A belief that may well be backward-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or belief held as true is a doctrine.
